titel: We eat with our eyes and ears
kurz: What we see and hear changes what we taste: colour raises expectations, and the crunch when biting makes crisps seem fresher.
bild_im_kopf: Like a film score: the same scene feels cheerful with happy music and menacing with dark music.
was_passiert: The brain builds taste from all the senses and fills gaps with expectations. In a well-known study, wine experts described white wine dyed red using terms for red wine. In another, crisps seemed crisper and fresher when the crunch sounded louder through headphones.
warum_wichtig: Explains why pale meat seems less flavoursome, why plating is more than decoration and why soggy chips disappoint even when they taste fine.
faustregeln: Colour is flavour: browning well pays off twice, for aroma and for expectation.
Add crunchy things just before serving so they audibly crunch.
Fresh herbs and a splash of colour at the end make a dish seem livelier.
